stories.headline: India, China hold high-level talks in Arunachal sector on border management, LAC issues: MEA
stories.title: India, China hold high-level talks in Arunachal sector on border management, LAC issues: MEA
stories.summary: MEA spokesperson Randhir also addressed a report claiming China-sourced satellite data may have aided Pakistan in tracking Indian troop movements and monitoring installations during Operation Sindoor
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Indian and Chinese armies held high-level talks this month in the Arunachal Pradesh sector focusing on border management and addressing outstanding issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

The talks, believed to have spread over a number of days, were held amid reports of aggressive military posturing by Chinese troops along the frontier, especially in the Upper Subansiri region of Arunachal Pradesh.
In September too, the senior military commanders of the two armies were engaged in flag talks in two sessions on both sides of the frontier in the Arunachal Pradesh sector.

“India and China engage regularly through diplomatic and military mechanisms and you are well aware of those mechanisms,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at his regular media briefing while responding to a question.
“A meeting of the senior military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently.
Discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management as well as addressing outstanding issues along the LAC,” he said.
Mr. Jaiswal said such interactions are aimed at maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas and preventing any escalation.

Lt. Gen Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Army’s III Corps headquartered near Dimapur in Nagaland, led the Indian delegation at the talks in the second week of this month, while the Chinese side was led by his counterpart.

In the military and diplomatic talks, India has been conveying to the Chinese side the importance of maintaining peace and tranquillity in the frontier regions for the continued development and progress of the overall bilateral relationship.

In the last one-and-a-half years, the two sides have taken a series of measures to rebuild their relationship after it came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in eastern Ladakh in 2020.

Nearly 50,000 troops of the Indian Army are deployed in various mountainous locations in eastern Ladakh, as multiple rounds of talks between the two sides have not yielded a concrete outcome to de-escalate the situation.
China has also deployed an equal number of troops, according to officials.

stories.headline: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
stories.title: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
stories.summary: Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court indicated orally on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) its inclination to set aside a Calcutta High Court order that put on hold the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections over a delimitation exercise, and requested the High Court to hear the dispute afresh.
A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the suggestion while hearing an appeal filed by the West Bengal government against the High Court order of November 6.
The High Court had directed the West Bengal State Election Commission to not notify the elections until a petition challenging the delimitation of municipal wards was decided.
Chief Justice Kant said the apex court was inclined to set aside the order of the High Court after taking into consideration pertinent legal and factual issues raised by the State government.
The writ petition could also be transferred from the Single Judge Bench to a Division Bench, which would consider the entire dispute afresh and pass appropriate orders.
“And till the Division Bench forms a view the polls can be held off,” the court suggested orally.
The lawyers for both the State and former CPI(M) councillor Dipu Das, who had filed the petition in the High Court against the delimitation exercise, sought time to take instructions.
The court listed the case for further hearing on November 30.
The Bench reasoned that its proposed “ad-hoc arrangement” would place both parties on an “even keel” without the Supreme Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the dispute.
The KMC had undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the civic polls.
As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144.

A Division Bench of the High Court had stopped the State Election Commission from issuing the election notification till the Single Judge Bench hearing Mr. Das’s petition decided the legality of the ward delimitation exercise.

stories.headline: Supreme Court nixes Allahabad HC order for Rahul’s assets probe
stories.title: Supreme Court nixes Allahabad HC order for Rahul’s assets probe
stories.summary: Supreme Court has quashed an order from the Allahabad high court to investigate Rahul Gandhi's assets. The high court did not consider Gandhi's response before issuing the order, which raised procedural concerns. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal criticized the order, claiming it permitted a witch-hunt without examining the petitioner's standing. The court will allow Gandhi to present his arguments regarding the petition's validity and the petitioner's status.

stories.headline: Why US is attacking Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat in new tariff threat
stories.title: Why US is attacking Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat in new tariff threat
stories.summary: Why US is attacking Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat in new tariff threat
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The US Trade Representative has determined that India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production are "unreasonable" and burden or restrict US commerce.
It has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, to which New Delhi has responded by rejecting the charge.
India is expanding factories, strengthening supply chains and developing domestic industries to increase its manufacturing capacity and establish itself as a major global manufacturing hub.
Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India) and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes have been central to that push.
But the Donald Trump administration took a very different reading of these policies.

Washington is arguing that India's drive for self-reliance risks producing too much manufacturing capacity and output, particularly when domestic demand does not keep pace with the factories being built.
That, US officials say, can push Indian companies towards export markets, where they compete with American manufacturers.
The Trump administration has used this argument to justify imposing tariffs on India.

The US Trade Representative has determined that India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production are "unreasonable" and burden or restrict US commerce under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.
It also claimed that a range of India's industrial and trade practices contribute to "structural excess capacity and production" and has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods.
The rate could be lowered to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a qualifying trade agreement.
Imagine a country builds factories capable of producing 100 units of a product when its domestic market needs only 60.

stories.headline: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for over 42 lakh farmers
stories.title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for over 42 lakh farmers
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Maharashtra Cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for over 42.30 lakh farmers not covered under Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), a ₹5,548-crore provision for the Narmada-Tapi diversion project in Nandurbar, confiscation of assets of firms involved in financial fraud, and a law to regulate private-aided schools, among 14 decisions.

At the meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, the Cabinet decided to give free foodgrains to farmers who are not covered under the National Food Security Act in 33 drought-affected districts of the State.
The beneficiaries belong to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category.
“The farmers will receive five kg of foodgrains per person every month, free of cost, for the next three months.
This will include three kg rice and two kg wheat,” stated a release issued from the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).
With an aim to strengthen the irrigation system in Nandurbar district, the Cabinet gave nod to the Narmada-Tapi diversion project.
This will include six diversions weirs that aim to benefit around 26,526 hectares with irrigation while generating 11.50 MW power, as per the Water Resources Department officials.
The Maharashtra government has also approved the plan to set up a separate MPID (Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors) tribunal with a time limit of 90 days for the disposal of cases.
The Cabinet also decided to expedite the process of confiscating properties of institutions committing financial fraud and amend the MPID Act,” stated the CMO.

The State government has also decided to increase the hostel allowances for students from Economically Weaker Sections (EBC, SEBC and EWS) pursuing professional degree courses in health sciences under the Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance Scheme.
It also approved the provision of financial facilities for teachers through RBI-registered institutions.
The Cabinet approved the draft Maharashtra Private-Aided Schools (Regulation) Bill, 2026, which will be tabled in the legislature.
